record.paper_title: Open problems on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers
record.original_question: In Euclidean dimension d>=3, is every maximal distance minimizer contained in a union of finitely many injective curves?

evidence.quote: Question 1.4. Is any MDM in R^d a union of a finite number of injective curves? Open for d≥3.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d \geq 3$ and let $M \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be a nonempty compact set, and let $r > 0$. A maximal distance minimizer for $(M, r)$ is a connected compact set $\Sigma \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ of minimal one-dimensional Hausdorff measure $\mathcal{H}^1(\Sigma)$ subject to the constraint
$$\max_{x \in M} \mathrm{dist}(x, \Sigma) \leq r,$$
where $\mathrm{dist}(x, \Sigma) = \inf_{y \in \Sigma} |x - y|$. An injective curve in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is the image of a continuous injective map $\gamma : [0,1] \to \mathbb{R}^d$.

Question: For every $d \geq 3$, every nonempty compact set $M \subset \mathbb{R}^d$, and every $r > 0$, is every maximal distance minimizer $\Sigma$ for $(M, r)$ contained in (equivalently, equal to) a union of finitely many injective curves?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is known in the plane ($d=2$): every planar maximal distance minimizer is a finite union of simple (injective) curves. For dimensions $d \geq 3$, the corresponding statement is recorded as an open problem in recent surveys and regularity papers on maximal distance minimizers.

status_evidence.title: An overview of maximal distance minimizers problem
status_evidence.snippet: Planar maximal distance minimizers are a finite union of simple curves; higher-dimensional regularity remains under investigation.
status_evidence.claim: The finite-union-of-curves result is established in the plane, while higher-dimensional regularity is still being studied.

status_evidence.title: On regularity of maximal distance minimizers in Euclidean Space
status_evidence.snippet: Studies tangent ray structure of maximal distance minimizers in R^n, showing at most 3 tangent rays per point with angles >= 2pi/3.
status_evidence.claim: Regularity of MDMs in R^d for d>=3 is only partially understood; the global structure as a finite union of injective curves is not established.
